info.title: SmartCura API
info.summary: Stage 0A foundation, identity, session and profile contract
info.description: Canonical REST contract. Firebase proves identity during session bootstrap, refresh and step-up; protected business routes use the opaque SmartCura session cookie.

get.summary: List broadcast messages
get.description: Organization-scoped. Requires the content:manage:organization permission.

post.summary: Compose a broadcast message
post.description: Binds the broadcast to one immutable template version.

put.summary: Schedule a broadcast message
put.description: Queues the broadcast through the transactional outbox for a future time.

post.summary: Send a broadcast message now
post.description: Queues the broadcast through the transactional outbox; the worker performs delivery.

get.summary: List organization custom roles
get.description: Requires the custom_role:manage:organization permission.

post.summary: Create a custom role
post.description: Derives from a system base role. Requires a valid step-up authentication window.

get.summary: List assignable permissions
get.description: The permission catalogue a custom role may receive. Global-scoped and wildcard permissions are excluded because the assign endpoint rejects them. Requires the custom_role:manage:organization permission.

put.summary: Update a custom role
put.description: Renames or deactivates a custom role under optimistic concurrency. Requires a valid step-up authentication window.

put.summary: Replace custom role permissions
put.description: Whole-set replacement. A permission outside the base role is rejected. Requires a valid step-up authentication window.

post.summary: Replay a dead-lettered outbox event
post.description: Privileged recovery action requiring system.security:*:global. Replay is idempotent: an already-replayed event is rejected with 409. Requires a valid step-up authentication window.

post.summary: Request a bulk data export
post.description: Records who asked and why, and requires recent step-up because an export is a bulk disclosure.

get.summary: Read export progress and availability
get.description: Reports whether the file is still downloadable; a file past its bounded lifetime is not.

get.summary: List FAQ entries
get.description: Organization-scoped. Requires the content:manage:organization permission.

post.summary: Create a FAQ entry
post.description: Organization-scoped. The slug must be unique inside the organization.

get.summary: Read one FAQ entry
get.description: Organization-scoped. Requires the content:manage:organization permission.

put.summary: Update a FAQ entry
put.description: Optimistic: expected_version must match the stored version.

delete.description: Soft archive. Published content history is never erased.

put.summary: Change FAQ publish state
put.description: Moves an entry between draft and published under optimistic concurrency.

get.summary: Read platform maintenance state
get.description: Global scope. Requires the platform.maintenance:manage:global permission. Never cached.

put.summary: Set platform maintenance state
put.description: Disabling maintenance must clear the reason and start time. Requires a valid step-up authentication window.

put.summary: Assign or clear a membership custom role
put.description: A null custom_role_id returns the membership to its system role. Requires a valid step-up authentication window.

200.description: Assign or clear a membership custom role

get.summary: List notification templates
get.description: Organization-scoped. Requires the content:manage:organization permission.

post.summary: Create a notification template
post.description: Creates the template and its first version.

put.summary: Activate a template version
put.description: Points the template at an existing version.

get.summary: List template versions
get.description: Template bodies are versioned; earlier versions are retained.

post.summary: Add a template version
post.description: Appends a new version without mutating an existing one.

get.summary: Read organization settings
get.description: Organization-scoped. Values are structured JSON with a reviewed key vocabulary.

put.summary: Update one organization setting
put.description: Optimistic: a first write expects version 0 and a later write must match the stored version.

get.summary: Read setting version history
get.description: Append-only history for one organization setting key. Never cached.

get.summary: Read an own or assigned-patient AI artifact
get.description: Authorized to the patient the artifact belongs to, or a doctor with an active care assignment. Anything else is a concealed 404, because whether an AI artifact exists for another patient is itself sensitive.

put.summary: Record an immutable doctor review decision
put.description: Requires ai.artifact:review:assigned plus an active care assignment, both re-proved under lock. Approving a replacement supersedes the prior approved version in the same transaction, so exactly one approved version is current. Review authority is doctor-only and is never inherited by an administrator.

post.summary: Start or resume the patient AI symptom conversation
post.description: Responses are no-store. Requires ai.conversation:manage:own on a patient membership.

post.summary: Submit a patient turn and queue a governed generation
post.description: Returns 202 with a queued generation. No model output is returned synchronously: the provider is called by the worker after commit, so no external latency is held inside a transaction. Repeating a client_correlation_id returns the original queued generation rather than generating twice.

503.description: No governed model or prompt template is available

get.summary: Read the artifact produced by a generation
get.description: Resolves a generation_id to its completed artifact. Returns 404 while the generation is still queued or running, so a client can poll this endpoint until the artifact is ready. Authorized to the patient who owns the generation, or a doctor with an active care assignment to that patient.

get.summary: List appointments visible to the authenticated actor
get.description: Returns the single scope the acting membership is entitled to: a patient sees their own appointments (appointment:read:own), a doctor the ones assigned to them (appointment:read:assigned), an administrator their organization's scheduling metadata (appointment:read:organization), and a super administrator global scheduling metadata (appointment:read:global). There is no cross-scope fallback and no way to request another actor's scope. Cursor pagination is deterministic on (created_at, appointment_id).

get.summary: Read one appointment
get.description: Authorized to the patient the appointment belongs to, the assigned doctor, an administrator in the appointment organization, or a super administrator with global metadata authority. An appointment outside the caller's scope is reported as 404 rather than 403: whether an appointment exists outside the allowed scope is itself sensitive, and a 403 would confirm it. Absence and denial are therefore indistinguishable.

post.summary: Create the one consultation for an eligible assigned appointment

put.summary: Create or replace the patient review for a completed appointment
put.description: Only the patient owning a completed appointment may review it. One row exists per appointment. expected_version=0 creates; matching version replaces; a same-version same-payload replay is returned unchanged.

post.summary: Reschedule an appointment onto another slot by replacement
post.description: Reschedule is by replacement, not mutation: the original keeps its time, fee and payment, moves to rescheduled and gains a link to the replacement, while a new appointment is booked against the new slot in the same transaction. The patient is therefore never charged twice. Requires both appointment:cancel:own and appointment:book:own, because a reschedule both cancels and books. expected_version guards the original and Idempotency-Key is mandatory; a replay returns the original response verbatim.

201.description: Replacement appointment, or the verbatim snapshot of an earlier request that used the same Idempotency-Key. A replayed snapshot carries the appointment representation only, without replaces_appointment_id.

put.summary: Cancel, check in, start, complete or record non-attendance
put.description: Patient authority permits pre-start cancellation and check-in; assigned-doctor authority permits pre-start cancellation, starting a checked-in appointment, completion from in_progress, and no-show after the scheduled start. Every command carries expected_version. State, role and scheduled-time guards are rechecked under lock; invalid transitions return APPOINTMENT_TRANSITION_INVALID. Reasons are structured and PHI-free.

schema.description: The reason code is bound to the target state: a cancellation reason may never be used for non-attendance and vice versa. Declared inline rather than as a named component so each concrete request keeps its own closed shape.

post.summary: Take a short-lived hold on a slot
post.description: Reserves a slot for five minutes so a patient can complete a booking without losing it. A hold is not a booking: it creates no appointment, has no address of its own and expires on its own, which is why the response is 200 rather than 201. An expired hold is reclaimed by the next booking transaction, so an abandoned checkout never removes capacity permanently. Requires appointment:book:own on a patient membership.

post.summary: Activate an emergency access grant
post.description: The controlled path by which a responder or doctor reads clinical data they hold no ordinary relationship to. Bounded to 15 minutes, tied to an active event and its patient, refused when the actor is the patient, and notified to security immediately. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: Read the minimum-necessary patient record
get.description: Grant validity and expiry are part of the query rather than a later comparison, so a clock check cannot be forgotten at a call site. Every disclosed field group is logged in the same transaction as the read. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: List vital readings under an active break-glass grant
get.description: Requires patient.record:read in the active session. The grant itself IS the object-level authority: an expired, terminated or foreign grant is concealed as 404. Every read is logged to break_glass_access_log with field_group = 'vital_readings' in the same transaction as the read. Newest first, cursor-paginated on (recorded_at, reading_id), optionally narrowed to one metric or a time window. Responses are never cached.

200.description: Page of vital readings, newest first

get.summary: List health alerts under an active break-glass grant
get.description: Requires patient.record:read in the active session. The grant itself IS the object-level authority: an expired, terminated or foreign grant is concealed as 404. Every read is logged to break_glass_access_log with field_group = 'health_alerts' in the same transaction as the read. Newest first, cursor-paginated on (observed_at, alert_id), optionally narrowed to one state. Responses are never cached.

200.description: Page of health alerts, newest first

post.summary: Record a retrospective review
post.description: Administrative capability, deliberately disjoint from activation so mutual sign-off between colleagues is not the normal path. Exactly one review per grant.

put.summary: Terminate an active grant
put.description: Records a structured termination reason and reports how many resources were accessed. Grant windows and justifications are immutable, so termination is the only permitted change.

get.summary: List care assignments visible to the active role
get.description: A patient receives assignments naming their profile; a doctor receives assignments naming the active clinician membership; an administrator receives organization assignments. A super-administrator must name organization_id. Scope cannot be selected by ordinary callers.

put.summary: Edit only an authored draft clinical note

get.summary: Read an owned or authored clinical note

post.summary: Create a signed replacement and supersede the prior signed note

put.summary: Sign or discard a draft clinical note

get.summary: List consent grants created by the authenticated patient
get.description: Patient-own scope only. Results are newest first and cursor paginated. Received grants and other patients are not exposed by this route.

post.summary: Grant consent over the authenticated patient records
post.description: Requires patient own authority. Exactly one profile or membership grantee is accepted. The grantee must be eligible and consent never replaces role permission or a care assignment.

post.summary: Revoke an active own consent grant
post.description: Revocation preserves history, requires optimistic expected_version and accepts only a structured reason.

get.summary: Read a participant consultation
Resolve the participant conversation
List participant-visible versioned clinical notes

post.summary: Create an assigned-doctor draft note

get.summary: List prescriptions created for a consultation

post.summary: Create an assigned-doctor draft prescription
Mint a short-lived participant-only room-scoped LiveKit token

put.summary: Apply a role- and state-guarded consultation transition

get.summary: Resume the persistent server-sequenced message feed

post.summary: Create a correlation-deduplicated participant message
post.description: Idempotency-Key must equal client_correlation_id. The server assigns sequence_no under the conversation lock; retrying the same payload returns the existing message, while reusing the correlation for different content returns MESSAGE_CORRELATION_REUSED. Sender identity always comes from the authenticated session.

put.summary: Persist participant receipts through a server sequence

post.summary: Rate an own completed delivery once

get.summary: Read recipient contact and address during an active assignment
get.description: Minimum-necessary disclosure, gated on the requesting driver holding an active assignment for the delivery. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: Read navigation stops during an active assignment
get.description: Ordered pickup and dropoff coordinates for the requesting driver's active assignment. A concealed 404 hides unknown ids, other drivers' assignments, and ended assignments alike. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: Read a single dispatch assignment owned by the calling driver
get.description: Returns the assignment summary (assignment id, job id, status, version, assigned and completed timestamps, fee). Concealed 404 for unknown ids and ids owned by other drivers, so the route cannot be used to confirm whether another driver's assignment exists at the same id. Responses are no-store.

put.summary: Advance an assignment one step, or cancel or fail it
put.description: Skipping a step is refused, so a delivery cannot complete without picked_up. Completion requires captured delivery proof, and a delivery fee is independently refused by the database unless the assignment is completed with proof.

post.summary: Report a location waypoint for an active assignment
post.description: Accepted at most once per interval unless flagged significant, which is always retained for route audit. Waypoints are append-only and must belong to an active assignment owned by the reporting driver.

get.summary: List open dispatch offers for the acting driver
get.description: Responses are no-store and carry no recipient identity. Driver identity is derived from the acting membership, never from the request.

post.summary: Accept an offer, creating the assignment and withdrawing competitors
post.description: Serializable because three conditions must hold at commit: the offer is still pending and unexpired, no sibling offer is accepted, and the driver holds no other active assignment. Partial unique indexes guarantee at most one accepted offer per job and one active assignment per driver, so concurrent acceptances yield exactly one winner and stable 409s for the rest.

get.summary: Search approved active doctors
get.description: Returns only active, approved doctor memberships with canonical professional detail. Query, specialty, language, fee, rating and accepting-new-patients filters are deterministic and cursor paginated.

get.summary: Read an approved doctor profile
get.description: Unapproved, inactive, missing-detail and unknown memberships are indistinguishable 404 responses. Includes two newest anonymous review previews.

get.summary: List anonymous verified-appointment reviews
get.description: Reviews never expose patient identity or appointment identifiers. Only reviews of an approved discoverable doctor are returned.

post.summary: Register a payout bank account
post.description: Own-scoped and step-up protected. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: Read the acting driver earnings balance
get.description: Projected over the append-only earnings ledger. Requires earning:read:own.

get.summary: List minimum-data ratings received by the acting driver
List the acting driver's own assignments
get.description: Ordered by urgency: active assignments a driver still owes progress on come first, then completed history. Cancelled and failed assignments are never returned. Driver identity is derived from the acting membership, never the request. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: List the acting driver vehicles

post.summary: Register an own vehicle

put.summary: Replace or deactivate an own vehicle

post.summary: Request a withdrawal of earned balance
post.description: Own-scoped and step-up protected. One in-flight withdrawal per driver.

get.summary: List emergency events
get.description: The dispatch queue for a site operator, gated on emergency.event:read:site — the same permission the per-event read uses, so the queue discloses nothing the detail view would not. Ordered by CLINICAL URGENCY, not recency: active events first, then critical before low, then oldest first within a priority. Recency ordering would put a new low-priority call above a critical one that has been waiting, which is the opposite of triage. The organization is taken from the caller’s membership, never from the request. Never cached.

parameters.name: active_only
parameters.description: Defaults to true: an operator opening the queue wants what is still happening.

post.summary: Raise an SOS emergency event
post.description: Creates the event, copies any supplied vital snapshots and queues notification in one transaction: an event that exists but was never announced is an emergency nobody is told about.

get.summary: Read an emergency event
get.description: Visible to the patient it concerns or an emergency membership in the same organization; anything else is a concealed 404.

post.summary: Record an emergency communication
post.description: Structured summary codes only, and only while the event is still active.

post.summary: Reserve an emergency unit
post.description: Atomic boundary 7. Reachable only from `triaged` or `dispatching`, because an untriaged event has no priority and choosing which unit to send is not yet a decision anyone can make.

post.summary: Resolve an emergency event
post.description: Requires notes, resolver and resolution type. The response duration is computed by the database from the event's own creation instant.

put.summary: Advance or terminate an emergency event
put.description: One step at a time, with cancellation and false alarm permitted from any live step. A terminal outcome releases the reserved unit and ends every break-glass grant the event justified.

post.summary: Record a triage assessment
post.description: Append-only evidence. The first assessment advances the event to `triaged`; later ones update priority without rewinding progress.

get.summary: Read projected ledger account balances
get.description: Read-only. Nothing on this route can move money; posting is a service capability granted to no interactive role. Responses are no-store.

get.summary: List posted ledger entries
get.description: Newest first. Requires ledger:read:organization. Never cached.

post.summary: Post a reversing entry
post.description: The only way to correct the ledger. The original entry is immutable and remains readable alongside its correction.

post.summary: Settle one payout line
post.description: Posts the balanced entry and marks the line paid in one transaction. Only while the run is processing, and only once.

get.summary: List payout runs
get.description: Newest period first: a payouts page is a record of what has been paid rather than a work queue. Requires payout_run:manage:organization rather than ledger:read:organization, because a payout run names its payees — reading it is payroll access, not general ledger access. Never cached.

post.summary: Prepare a doctor payout run
post.description: Creates a draft batch. Amounts remain editable only while the run is draft.

post.summary: Add a payee line to a draft run
post.description: Refused once the run is approved, because approval must guarantee the total someone signed for.

put.summary: Approve, start or cancel a payout run
put.description: Separation of duties is enforced by role AND by person: the preparer cannot approve their own batch.

put.summary: Review, settle, fail or cancel a driver withdrawal
put.description: Mounted under finance rather than `/drivers/me` because reviewing somebody else's payout is not a self-service action, and a path should say who is acting.

get.summary: Process liveness

post.summary: Acknowledge a health alert
post.description: Requires alert:acknowledge:assigned, granted to doctor only. No MFA step-up: acknowledging is the ordinary work of a shift and a fresh challenge would delay the response to a critical alert, which is the opposite of what the alert is for. The alert is addressed directly and neither its organization nor its patient appears in the path, because both are properties of the stored row and a caller-supplied value could disagree with it; the server reads the alert to learn both and conceals every mismatch as 404. The care assignment is proved before anything is disclosed and then proved AGAIN inside the transaction under a share lock on the assignment rows, so a clinician whose assignment ended in between cannot acknowledge — that outcome is CARE_ASSIGNMENT_REQUIRED. The acting membership is recorded as the acknowledging clinician, because an assignment belongs to a membership rather than to a profile. No Idempotency-Key: expected_version makes a repeated acknowledgement HEALTH_ALERT_VERSION_CONFLICT rather than a second clinical act, an already-acknowledged alert is returned unchanged rather than as an error, and a resolved alert is HEALTH_ALERT_NOT_OPEN.

200.description: Alert after the acknowledgement, or unchanged when it was already acknowledged at the supplied version

put.summary: Escalate, resolve or dismiss an assigned health alert
put.description: Responses are no-store. resolved and dismissed are terminal, so a closed alert can never reopen. An escalation appends an immutable health_alert_escalations record carrying actor, recipient and reason.

get.summary: List the medication catalogue

post.summary: Create a medication catalogue entry
post.description: Pharmacy-only and step-up protected because the command may classify a controlled substance.

get.summary: Read a medication catalogue entry

put.summary: Replace a medication catalogue entry
put.description: Optimistic and step-up protected; controlled_substance is derived from controlled_schedule.

post.summary: Record a per-date availability exception for the acting doctor
post.description: Closes the bookable slots the exception invalidates and regenerates the day when a replacement window is supplied. Booked capacity is never withdrawn silently: the database refuses to release a slot with a live appointment on it, so the doctor must cancel those appointments explicitly. The write is an upsert on (membership, date) guarded by expected_version. The reason code is a structured PHI-free enum, never free text, because it reaches audit logs and patient-facing copy. Requires availability:write:own.

201.description: Stored exception with the number of slots closed and regenerated

get.summary: Read the acting doctor's weekly availability rule set
get.description: Returns the active rules and the revision to quote back as expected_version on a replacement. Authorized by availability:write:own rather than a read permission: a rule set is the doctor's own working pattern plus the concurrency token that lets it be rewritten, not published capacity, and availability:read:global exposes slots only. The membership in the path must be the acting membership; any other is concealed as 404. Responses are never cached.

200.description: Active rule set with the revision to present on the next replacement

put.summary: Replace the acting doctor's weekly availability rule set
put.description: Replaces the entire active rule set for the doctor's own membership and regenerates the bookable slot horizon in the same transaction. Replacement rather than a partial update because a recurrence set has no safe merge rule: two clients each patching a different weekday would both succeed without seeing the other's day, and the result is immediately materialised into slots patients can pay for. Requires availability:write:own; the membership in the path must be the acting membership and any other is concealed as 404. Overlapping windows on one weekday are rejected as VALIDATION_FAILED, and a stale expected_version as AVAILABILITY_VERSION_CONFLICT.

200.description: Replacement rule set with the new revision and the number of slots generated

get.summary: Read already-generated bookable slots for the acting doctor's own schedule
get.description: Requires availability:read:own, granted to doctor. The membership in the path must be the acting membership; a mismatch is concealed as a 404. Every slot state is returned — open, held, booked and closed — because a doctor reviewing their own schedule needs to see it as it actually is, not just the bookable capacity the organization search publishes. Cursor-paginated on (starts_at, slot_id), bounded to a 62-day window. Responses are never cached.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on starts_at, as an absolute instant with an explicit offset

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound on starts_at; strictly after from, within a 62-day window

200.description: Page of the doctor's own availability slots over the requested range, earliest first

post.summary: Generate the acting doctor's bookable slots over a date range
post.description: Materialises slots from the existing active rule set over an inclusive local date range, for a doctor publishing capacity further ahead than the last rule replacement reached. Generation is idempotent in the database — every insert conflicts away against the live-slot uniqueness index, so it cannot duplicate a slot or disturb a held or booked one — and days carrying an exception are skipped. Idempotency-Key is mandatory nonetheless, because a retry would otherwise honestly report zero new slots and a client would read that as failure; a replay returns the original stored count verbatim. Requires availability:write:own. A membership with no active rule is AVAILABILITY_RULES_MISSING.

201.description: Slots generated, or the verbatim snapshot of an earlier request that used the same Idempotency-Key

get.summary: Read the professional detail for a doctor membership
get.description: Own membership, or an approved public view. The fee published here is the only price a booking may charge.

put.summary: Create or replace own professional detail
put.description: Own membership only. Specialties and languages are replaced as a set, and money is integer MYR sen.

get.summary: List the verification documents of one membership
get.description: Readable by the profile that owns the membership, and by an organization administrator or platform administrator through their review authority. A caller with neither authority receives 404 rather than 403, because 403 would confirm that the membership exists.

post.summary: Request an upload target for a verification document
post.description: Creates the document and its pending stored-object metadata, then returns a short-lived upload capability for a server-derived object key. The bytes travel client to store directly and are not trusted until finalize proves the checksum; nothing is reviewable and nothing is downloadable before then. Approving a document never activates a membership.

201.description: Document reserved with a short-lived upload target. A replayed idempotent request returns the stored document with a freshly minted target, because a pre-signed capability cannot be replayed after it expires.

get.summary: Request a short-lived download capability for a verification file
get.description: Returns a 60-second no-store GET capability only after the caller is re-authorized against the linked verification document. The owner may read their own file; an organization administrator may read files in their organization; a platform super-administrator may read globally. Unrelated callers receive the same 404 as an absent document. Finalized, checksum-matched and clean are all required; pending, infected, quarantined, rejected, deleted and scan-failed objects are never signed.

Cache-Control.description: Private capabilities and file metadata must never be cached.

post.summary: Confirm the uploaded bytes of a verification document
post.description: Three digests must agree: the one declared when the upload was requested, the one reported here, and the one the store itself holds. The store's answer is the one a client cannot forge, so a key the store does not know, or holds without a checksum, is treated as a mismatch. A mismatch moves the object to a terminal rejected state that can never be downloadable, and a new upload must be requested.

200.description: Document finalized; the stored object now carries a verified checksum and awaits the malware scan

get.summary: List authoritative in-app notifications newest first

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Filter to one category.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: Filter to unread (true) or read (false) notifications.

put.summary: Mark every unread notification of the caller as read
put.description: Scoped to the calling profile in the repository WHERE clause, so one account can never clear another's badge. Returns { "updated": n }.

put.summary: Persist independent in-app read state

get.summary: List own notification preferences

put.summary: Update future push delivery and quiet-hour behavior

post.summary: Register a server-managed push device for the authenticated profile
post.description: Responses are no-store. Re-registering the same token re-binds and re-enables one row rather than creating duplicates.

put.summary: Disable an owned push device so future push delivery stops

get.summary: Search an organization's bookable slots
get.description: Published capacity only: no patient identity, hold owner or appointment detail is returned. Only slots whose doctor a booking would actually accept are listed — active doctor membership, approved verification, accepting new patients — because advertising capacity that booking refuses under lock sends every patient down a path ending in 409. Optionally narrowed to one doctor with membership_id. Authorized by availability:read:global, granted broadly because a patient must see bookable capacity before any relationship exists to scope it by. The window is bounded at 62 days and cursor pagination is deterministic on (starts_at, slot_id). A listed slot is never proof of bookability: the booking transaction re-proves the doctor and the slot under lock.

parameters.name: membership_id
parameters.description: Narrows the search to one doctor membership

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive window start as an absolute instant with an explicit offset

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive window end; strictly after from and at most 62 days later

post.summary: Book an appointment from a held or open slot
post.description: Idempotency-Key is mandatory and a client never supplies the price. The transaction locks the slot, revalidates the active approved doctor, serializes the patient schedule, rejects overlapping live appointments, and creates exactly one appointment. Zero-fee bookings confirm immediately. Positive-fee bookings create a pending simulated payment intent plus appointment.payment-requested.v1; the worker settles it after commit, so no provider call occurs while booking locks are held. Retry returns the original stored response.

201.description: Appointment booked, or the verbatim snapshot of an earlier request that used the same Idempotency-Key

post.summary: Assign an approved doctor to an active patient
post.description: Requires organization/global administration permission and current MFA step-up. The doctor must be active and approved in the same organization. A partial unique index prevents concurrent duplicate active assignments.

post.summary: Complete or revoke an active care assignment
post.description: Requires organization/global administration permission, current MFA step-up, optimistic expected_version and a structured PHI-free reason. History is closed, never deleted.

get.summary: List the organization's IoT devices
get.description: Requires device:read:organization. A device is owned by exactly one organization and the identifier in the path must be the acting membership's own; any other value is concealed as 404 so the route cannot be walked to discover which organizations exist. The optional state filter is the device LIFECYCLE, not connectivity: a reachable but suspended device is still suspended and may not ingest, while reachability is last_seen_at, which only ingestion writes. Cursor pagination is deterministic on (created_at, device_id) — created_at alone is not unique, so a bulk import that registered two devices in the same millisecond would repeat or skip one at the page boundary. Responses are never cached: a device body carries its serial number and the patient currently assigned to it.

200.description: Page of devices, each with its open assignment if it has one

post.summary: Register an IoT device into the organization
post.description: Requires device:register:organization and a current MFA step-up: provisioning hardware mints a broker credential, so a stolen idle session must not be able to do it. The body carries provisioning_secret in PLAINTEXT and this is the only request in which it ever appears — the server hashes it to a SHA-256 lowercase hex digest, stores only the digest in device_credentials, and never logs it, echoes it in the response, writes it to audit metadata or folds it into the idempotency request fingerprint, so neither a database disclosure nor a leak of the idempotency ledger can be replayed against the broker. The operator must keep the plaintext at provisioning time because it is unrecoverable afterwards. Idempotency-Key is mandatory: the key is claimed inside the registration transaction, so a retry returns the stored response of the original request instead of colliding with the per-organization serial-number uniqueness index and leaving the operator unsure which attempt won. A serial number already registered in the organization is DEVICE_SERIAL_NUMBER_CONFLICT.

201.description: Device registered, or the verbatim snapshot of an earlier request that used the same Idempotency-Key. The response never contains the provisioning secret or its digest.

get.summary: Read one IoT device
get.description: Requires device:read:organization. The lookup is scoped by organization, so a device owned by another organization is reported as absent rather than forbidden: absence and concealment are indistinguishable by design, because confirming that a serial exists elsewhere is itself a disclosure. The representation always carries at most one open assignment, which a partial unique index guarantees however long the release history is. version is the value to quote back as expected_version on an assignment or release.

200.description: Device with its open assignment if it has one

post.summary: Assign an IoT device to a patient
post.description: Requires device:assign:organization and a current MFA step-up: this decides which patient a stream of clinical measurements is attributed to, and an alert raised from a misattributed reading reaches the wrong clinician. 200 rather than 201 because the assignment has no address of its own and the response is the device it changed. At most one assignment may be open per device, enforced by a partial unique index rather than by a read-then-write, so two concurrent requests cannot both succeed and the loser is DEVICE_ALREADY_ASSIGNED. A suspended or retired device is DEVICE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE — readings from it would otherwise be accepted by a path that believes the device is trusted. A stale expected_version is DEVICE_VERSION_CONFLICT, and a profile that cannot hold an assignment at all is VALIDATION_FAILED. Assigning moves a provisioned device to active.

post.summary: Release an IoT device from its current patient
post.description: Requires device:assign:organization and a current MFA step-up, for the same reason as assignment. A sub-resource action rather than a DELETE because nothing is removed: the open row is closed with a timestamp and a structured PHI-free reason code and the history stays intact, since a reading recorded last month must remain attributable to the patient the device was assigned to then. The reason is an enum and never free text, because it lands in a broadly retained audit log and in append-only history where clinical detail typed into an open field can never be withdrawn. No Idempotency-Key: expected_version already makes a repeated release DEVICE_VERSION_CONFLICT rather than a second release, and a device with no open assignment is DEVICE_NOT_ASSIGNED.

post.summary: Submit a batch of vital readings from one device
post.description: Requires reading:ingest:device, held by admin (submitting on behalf of a gateway or the simulator) and by patient (submitting from a device assigned to them). No MFA step-up: ingestion is the routine act the subsystem exists for, and a step-up requirement would either drop clinical data or teach people to keep elevated sessions open permanently. The patient is never in the request: attribution is resolved server side from the device's open assignment, exactly as the MQTT vitals packet forbids patient_id, and a patient actor may only submit for the device currently assigned to them. There is deliberately NO Idempotency-Key. Each reading carries its own packet identity (device, boot_id, sequence_number) and the unpartitioned vital_reading_ingest_claims table holds that as a primary key claimed in the same transaction as the insert, so a redelivered packet stores nothing, raises no alert and is counted as deduplicated — per reading, at any batch boundary. A request-level header keys on whole requests instead, so a buffer resent with different batching would present a new key and be treated as fresh: a second, weaker mechanism closing no hole the ledger leaves open. 202 rather than 201 because the response classifies the batch and a routine batch is part accepted, part deduplicated, part rejected — a reading older than the 30-day replay window, or more than five minutes ahead of server time, is rejected rather than stored. Thresholds are evaluated in the same transaction, so an alert exists if and only if the reading that raised it does. A suspended or retired device is DEVICE_NOT_INGESTIBLE and a device with no open assignment is DEVICE_NOT_ASSIGNED.

reported_sha256.description: What the client claims it uploaded. Not sufficient on its own: it must agree with the digest declared at request time and with the digest the store reports.

status.description: not_submitted and pending_review are not reviewer outcomes; rejected and expired are terminal and are re-established by a new submission.

expected_version.description: Optimistic concurrency. A stale reviewer is rejected rather than allowed to overwrite a newer decision, which is also what makes a repeated review harmless.

LocalTime.description: Wall-clock time local to the rule's timezone, as HH:MM or HH:MM:SS

AppointmentPaymentState.description: Positive-fee bookings create a pending simulated payment intent. The outbox worker settles it after the booking transaction commits; capture confirms the appointment and failure cancels it. A refundable pre-start cancellation moves captured to refunded.

AppointmentCancellationReasonCode.description: Structured, PHI-free cancellation reasons. Free text is not accepted because the reason reaches audit logs, the other party's appointment view and the published event, and no caller can be relied upon to keep clinical detail out of an open string field.

AppointmentNoShowReasonCode.description: Non-attendance findings, recorded by the assigned doctor only

AppointmentReasonCode.description: Every code the stored reason field can hold: a cancellation reason, a non-attendance finding, or rescheduled, which a reschedule stamps on the appointment it replaces. Read-only; requests use the narrower enum bound to the state they ask for.

AvailabilityExceptionReasonCode.description: Structured, PHI-free reasons a doctor closes or moves a working day

end_time.description: Strictly after start_time, and the window length must be an exact multiple of slot_duration_minutes

effective_to.description: Open ended when null; otherwise on or after effective_from

data.description: The active rules only; superseded revisions are not returned

version.description: The revision to present as expected_version on the next replacement. Present even when the rule list is empty, because withdrawing all capacity still advances the revision.

rules.description: The complete replacement rule set. An empty array withdraws all future unbooked capacity.

expected_version.description: Optimistic concurrency check against the stored rule-set revision; 0 for a doctor who has never published rules

horizon_days.description: How far ahead slots are generated from now

is_unavailable.description: True closes the day and forbids a replacement window; false requires both replacement times

closed_slot_count.description: Open and held slots closed on that date; booked slots are never withdrawn silently

to_date.description: Inclusive end of the range: on or after from_date and at most 120 days later, the same span a rule replacement may generate

generated_slot_count.description: Slots newly created. Zero is a legitimate answer when the range was already materialised; a replay reports the original count instead.

version.description: The rule-set revision the slots were generated from

state.description: A slot listed as bookable is open, or held by a hold that has already lapsed

BookAppointmentRequest.description: There is deliberately no fee field. The consultation fee is read from the doctor's own record under lock inside the booking transaction; a client-supplied price would let the patient choose what to pay, and additionalProperties: false makes sending one a validation failure rather than a silent no-op.

Appointment.description: The single appointment representation, used for live responses and for the stored idempotency snapshot, so a replay is identical by construction. fee_sen and currency mirror the components of Money as flat fields because that is the wire shape the server emits; the fee is server-derived and a client never supplies either field.

fee_sen.description: Integer MYR sen, taken from the doctor's own consultation fee under lock at booking time

payment_state.description: Null when the fee is zero and no payment aggregate was created

cancellation_reason_code.description: The structured reason recorded with the last cancellation, non-attendance or reschedule

replaced_by_appointment_id.description: Set on a rescheduled appointment, pointing at its replacement

RescheduledAppointment.description: The replacement appointment plus the identifier of the appointment it replaced. The properties are restated rather than composed with allOf because Appointment sets additionalProperties: false, which no allOf branch may extend under JSON Schema 2020-12. replaces_appointment_id is present on a fresh reschedule and absent on an idempotent replay, because the stored snapshot is the appointment representation alone and a replay must reproduce it byte for byte.

replaces_appointment_id.description: The appointment that moved to rescheduled and keeps the original time, fee and payment. Omitted on an idempotent replay.

CompleteAppointmentRequest.description: Completion takes no reason code at all: a completed appointment has nothing to explain, and the database forbids one.

slot_id.description: The new slot. It must be a different slot: a slot is single-use forever.

mode.description: Null keeps the original appointment's mode

DeviceState.description: The device lifecycle, not its connectivity. A reachable but suspended device is still suspended and may not ingest; reachability is last_seen_at.

DeviceCredentialType.description: Which kind of credential the provisioning secret is. Only its SHA-256 digest is ever stored.

DeviceReleaseReasonCode.description: Structured PHI-free reasons for releasing a device. Free text is deliberately not accepted: the reason reaches broadly retained audit logs and an append-only assignment history, where clinical detail cannot be withdrawn.

DeviceAssignment.description: The device's OPEN assignment. At most one exists at a time, guaranteed by a partial unique index, however long the release history is.

Device.description: The single device representation, used for live responses and for the stored idempotency snapshot, so a replayed registration is identical by construction. No credential material appears here: only the SHA-256 digest of the provisioning secret is stored, and even that is never returned.

serial_number.description: Compared for equality against a physical label, so case and padding are constrained: a lowercase spelling of the same device would register twice and no operator could tell the two apart.

last_seen_at.description: Connectivity, written only by ingestion. Null until the device has submitted a reading.

active_assignment.description: Null when the device is not currently assigned to a patient

RegisterDeviceRequest.description: provisioning_secret is the plaintext credential the device will present to the broker, and this is the only request in which it ever appears. The server hashes it to SHA-256 lowercase hex, stores only the digest, and never logs it, echoes it, writes it to audit metadata or folds it into the idempotency request fingerprint. It is unrecoverable afterwards, so the operator must keep it at provisioning time.

serial_number.description: Unique within the organization. The same pattern the database enforces, so a mis-cased or padded label is a validation failure rather than a duplicate registration.

provisioning_secret.description: Plaintext broker credential, printable ASCII with no spaces. Write-only: it is never present in any response.

patient_profile_id.description: The patient the device's readings will be attributed to. The profile must be active with onboarding completed.

expected_version.description: Optimistic concurrency version from the last read. When omitted, the service reads the current version from the unassigned device.

VitalMetric.description: The measured quantity. Each metric has exactly one canonical unit and one value range, both enforced by the database: a heart rate labelled Cel would otherwise be charted as a temperature.

VitalReadingQuality.description: The instrument's own confidence. A bad reading is stored for the record but excluded from rollups and never raises an alert: waking a clinician for a measurement the instrument rejected trains people to ignore alerts.

VitalReadingSample.description: One reading as the device reports it. boot_id counts power cycles and sequence_number counts readings within a boot; together with the device they form the packet identity the ingest claim ledger deduplicates on, which is why both are mandatory and non-negative — a wrapped or tampered counter makes the identity untrustworthy. unit must be the metric's canonical unit and value must lie inside the metric's range, so a self-contradictory sample is a validation failure rather than a constraint violation that aborts the batch.

unit.description: UCUM code, and part of the measurement rather than a display hint. It must be the canonical unit for the metric: /min for heart_rate and respiratory_rate, % for oxygen_saturation, Cel for body_temperature, mm[Hg] for blood_pressure/systolic_bp/diastolic_bp, mg/dL for blood_glucose, kg for body_weight, mV for ecg_voltage.

recorded_at.description: When the device measured it, as an absolute instant with an explicit offset. A bare local timestamp is rejected: a reading time means nothing without a zone, and guessing one would land the row in the wrong monthly partition. Readings older than the 30-day replay window or more than five minutes ahead of server time are rejected.

IngestVitalReadingsRequest.description: A batch upload. There is no patient field: attribution comes from the device's open assignment, never from the client. The lower bound of one rejects an empty submission, which is indistinguishable from a client bug; the upper bound of 200 keeps one transaction — claims, readings, rollups, threshold evaluation and outbox rows — inside a predictable amount of work, since a device replaying an offline buffer would otherwise send its whole day at once.

AcceptedVitalReading.description: A reading stored by this call, echoed so a device can retire it from its own buffer

VitalReadingIngestOutcome.description: How the batch was classified. patient_profile_id is the attribution the server resolved from the device's open assignment, returned so the submitter can confirm it rather than choose it. The three counts always sum to the number of submitted readings.

deduplicated.description: Readings whose packet identity was already claimed. A fully replayed batch reports every reading here and stores nothing, which is the observable proof that at-least-once redelivery cannot duplicate clinical data.

rejected.description: Readings outside the accepted replay window or the tolerated clock lead. A packet past the window cannot be proved unseen, because the claim that would catch the duplicate may already have been purged.

alerts_raised.description: Alerts opened by this batch. A breach sustained across many readings opens one alert, not one per reading.

VitalReading.description: One stored reading. The measured value is returned only on an authorized read; the published vital_reading.changed.v1 event carries the identity, metric, quality and time but never the value, because an event stream fans out far more widely than an authorized read.

ingested_at.description: When the server stored it. Never earlier than recorded_at, so offline-replay lag stays measurable instead of negative.

HealthAlert.description: One breach of one threshold by one reading. At most one alert is live per patient, metric and threshold, so a sustained breach does not bury the first alert under identical ones. observed_value is clinical data and is deliberately excluded from every published event payload.

observed_value.description: The measured value that breached the threshold

threshold_id.description: The threshold that was breached. A patient-scoped threshold overrides the organization default for the same metric, comparator and severity, and retiring the override restores the default.

observed_at.description: The recorded time of the reading that raised the alert, not the time the alert was written

acknowledged_by_profile_id.description: Set together with acknowledged_at, never separately: an acknowledgement without an acknowledger is an unauditable clinical action

resolved_at.description: Non-null exactly when state is resolved

AcknowledgeHealthAlertRequest.description: expected_version is the whole request: there is nothing for a clinician to choose when acknowledging, and the version is what makes a repeated acknowledgement a conflict rather than a second clinical act.

url.description: A 60-second signed capability. It is never persisted, cached or logged.

required_headers.description: Provider-owned headers that must accompany the signed request.

ClinicalNoteContent.description: Versioned structured clinical note content; bounded to 65536 serialized bytes.

CreateMessageRequest.description: For text, text_content is required and file_object_id omitted; for file, file_object_id is required and text_content omitted. The API enforces this discriminated shape strictly.

RegisterPushDeviceRequest.description: The registration token is a provider credential. It is stored encrypted, indexed only by hash, and is never returned by any response or published in any event.

ReadingSource.description: Origin of the reading. A manually entered value is never presented as an instrument measurement.

TransitionHealthAlertRequest.description: Escalates, resolves or dismisses an alert. Only an escalation may name a recipient membership. Requires iot.alert:escalate:assigned plus an active care assignment, both re-proved under lock.

AiArtifactSource.description: A knowledge citation referenced by an AI artifact.

AiArtifactContent.description: Non-diagnostic clinical-support content. non_diagnostic must be true; the database CHECK rejects an artifact without it, so a client cannot receive unlabelled output.

AiArtifact.description: A governed, non-diagnostic clinical-support artifact. Content and provenance are immutable; a rerun creates a new version. AI output never changes diagnosis, medication, alert, appointment or emergency state.

confidence.description: Present only when the producing model defines and validates a calibrated score. An LLM self-reported certainty is forbidden, so LLM artifacts always report null.

SubmitAiTurnRequest.description: A patient turn. role, model, prompt template, risk level, confidence and review status are server facts and are rejected if supplied.

InventoryAvailability.description: Every quantity is DERIVED as posted ledger movements minus active reservations. No stored balance exists, because a stored balance is what makes overselling possible.

ValidatePharmacyOrderRequest.description: Validation and FEFO reservation are ONE command (atomic boundary 4). A non-valid outcome requires a reason code; a valid outcome carries none.

PharmacyValidationResult.description: A valid prescription with insufficient stock ends at validated with the unfillable items named, never at stock_reserved and never silently short-filled.

TransitionPharmacyOrderRequest.description: Fulfilment progress only. Reservation and dispatch are separate commands because each is its own atomic boundary. Cancelling releases active holds.

version.description: Optimistic-concurrency version. Echoed back as `expected_version` when accepting the offer.

DispatchOfferSummary.description: Minimum-necessary offer. Recipient name, phone, address and precise coordinates are absent by construction: they live on the delivery record, not the offer, so a driver browsing offers cannot harvest patient contact details.

AdvanceAssignmentRequest.description: Progress is strictly one step at a time, so a delivery cannot complete without picked_up ever occurring. Completion additionally requires captured delivery proof. Only cancellation or failure carries a reason code.

DispatchStop.description: One planned stop of a dispatch job. Coordinates are decimal-degree strings, matching the PatientAddress coordinate convention.

DispatchAssignmentStops.description: Disclosed ONLY while the requesting driver holds an active assignment. The ownership and active-status join is part of the query, so a driver whose assignment ended reads nothing rather than stale coordinates. Anything else is a concealed 404.

DispatchAssignmentSummary.description: A driver's own assignment row. The fee is joined from the dispatch job, so it can never disagree with the job it serves. Recipient identity and address are absent; they are disclosed only through the active-assignment recipient endpoint.

RecipientDisclosure.description: Disclosed ONLY while the requesting driver holds an active assignment for this delivery. The relationship is part of the query, so a driver whose assignment ended reads nothing rather than stale details. Anything else is a concealed 404.

RecordWaypointRequest.description: recorded_at is the device clock; received_at is stamped by the server, so a client cannot backdate arrival. Coordinates are bounded decimals: PostGIS is not yet enabled on the runtime image.

WaypointOutcome.description: throttled is a normal outcome, not an error: reporting more often than the interval is expected client behaviour, and returning an error would make drivers retry and amplify the load the throttle exists to reduce.

DriverEarnings.description: Balance projected over the append-only earnings ledger; no stored wallet field exists. A delivery fee is only postable for a completed assignment carrying proof.

ProfileDetailReasonCode.description: Structured reason code. Free text is never accepted: audit rows are retained broadly, and a free-text field beside an allergy or condition is the likeliest route for clinical detail to leak into them.

PatientAddress.description: Coordinates stay decimal STRINGS end to end, matching the numeric column: parsing to float and re-serializing would change the stored value for some inputs. Latitude and longitude are supplied together or not at all, since half a pair is not a location.

PatientAllergy.description: Attribution is derived from the authenticated session; noted_by_profile_id is never accepted from a request, because that would let a patient attribute their own entry to a clinician who never saw it.

PatientCondition.description: A resolved_date requires status resolved and may not precede onset_date, mirroring the column check so the two definitions of "resolved" cannot drift.

DoctorProfessionalDetail.description: Money is an integer count of MYR sen and currency is not a request field: accepting one would imply the platform can price in something else.

EmergencyEventStatus.description: Lifecycle state only. Triage priority is a SEPARATE field: the portal values critical/dispatched/pending mixed the two, and merging urgency with progress makes an escalating patient indistinguishable from an advancing response.

TriagePriority.description: `unknown` is the absence of assessment, never its outcome, so it cannot be submitted as a triage result.

metric.description: Canonical metric names. `spo2` and `ecg_sample` were renamed to `oxygen_saturation` and `ecg_voltage`; the old names are not accepted.

unit.description: Must be the canonical unit for the metric: `/min` heart rate and respiratory rate, `%` oxygen saturation, `Cel` body temperature, `mm[Hg]` blood pressure, `mg/dL` blood glucose, `kg` body weight, `mV` ECG voltage.

quality.description: Canonical trust vocabulary. `good`/`bad` were renamed to `valid`/`invalid`, because a reading is trusted or not rather than qualitatively good.

EmergencyVitalSnapshot.description: A point-in-time COPY of the vitals that justified the call, not a reference to a live reading. A later correction or deletion of the reading must not rewrite what the responders acted on.

patient_profile_id.description: Omit for oneself. Naming another patient requires a live consent grant: without that check anyone could manufacture an emergency event for any profile, and an active event is exactly the precondition a break-glass grant needs.

RaiseEmergencyRequest.description: The reporter is always the authenticated session and is never accepted from the body. Coordinates are supplied together or not at all.

EmergencyEventView.description: Readable by the patient the event concerns, or an emergency membership in the same organization. Any other caller receives 404 rather than 403, since confirming an emergency exists is itself a disclosure.

RecordTriageRequest.description: Append-only: a priority change is new evidence, never an overwrite. Re-triaging an already dispatched event updates the priority WITHOUT rewinding lifecycle state, because a worsening patient must not reset an en-route response.

ReserveUnitRequest.description: A manual override of automatic selection is a reviewable act and must state why; only an override may carry a reason. Validated here so an unexplained override is a 422 rather than a constraint violation surfacing as a 500.

EmergencyDispatchCreated.description: Atomic boundary 7: reserving the unit, creating the dispatch and transitioning the event commit in ONE serializable transaction. Partial unique indexes independently guarantee one active dispatch per event and per unit, so two operators assigning the last ambulance produce one reservation.

AdvanceEmergencyRequest.description: One step at a time along created→triaged→dispatching→unit_assigned→responding→on_scene, then transporting→resolved or resolved directly, so an event cannot reach `responding` with no triage recorded. `cancelled` and `false_alarm` may interrupt any live step and require a reason. A terminal outcome releases the unit and ends every break-glass grant justified by the event, in the same commit.

ResolveEmergencyRequest.description: Notes, resolver and resolution type are all required. Clinical outcome labels such as stable or deceased belong in `outcome_code`, not in the lifecycle state.

EmergencyResolution.description: The duration is a GENERATED column computed from the event's own creation instant and checked by a deferred trigger. It is never accepted from a client, because a self-reported response time is the one number an operator would be tempted to improve.

RecordCommunicationRequest.description: Structured summary only. Verbatim call content would put unbounded clinical narrative into a table that is later read under break-glass.

renews_grant_id.description: A renewal is a NEW grant superseding the named one, never an extension: policy requires a fresh reason and event record per renewal, and an updatable expiry would make an indefinite grant look like a single short access.

ActivateBreakGlassRequest.description: The patient is taken from the EVENT, not the request. Requires an active doctor or emergency membership holding BOTH `break_glass:activate` AND the underlying `patient.record:read` — activation alone is never read authority — plus recent step-up authentication.

BreakGlassGrant.description: Bounded to at most 15 minutes by a database CHECK, so a service bug cannot mint a longer window. Activation emits an immediate security notification through the outbox and writes its first audit entry in the same transaction.

BreakGlassDisclosure.description: Minimum-necessary projection: life-threatening allergies first, unresolved conditions only, and no notes, history, files, AI artifacts or finance. Every field group disclosed is written to an append-only access log in the SAME transaction as the read, so a crash cannot produce an unrecorded disclosure. An expired, terminated or foreign grant returns 404.

ReviewBreakGlassRequest.description: Requires `break_glass:review`, which is seeded only to administrative roles; a migration assertion fails if any role holds both activate and review. The actor is read from the grant, so the not-self rule cannot be defeated by supplying another identity, and it is independently a database CHECK.

LedgerAccountBalance.description: The balance is PROJECTED over signed postings and is not stored anywhere. A stored balance would be a second source of truth that eventually disagrees with the ledger, and the ledger has to win.

LedgerReversal.description: A correction is a NEW entry that mirrors every posting of the original with the opposite sign. The original is never edited, so the trail shows both what happened and what corrected it. At most one reversal per entry, so a single mistake cannot be corrected twice into a windfall.

CreatePayoutRunRequest.description: One open run per period, so two half-built batches cannot both claim the same weeks.

AddPayoutItemRequest.description: The payee PROFILE is resolved from the membership within this organization and is never accepted from the request, because a run that could name any profile would move money to someone no approval step would notice. Money is integer MYR sen.

PayoutItemCreated.description: `net_sen` is a generated column, gross minus fee, so the arithmetic cannot drift from its inputs.

AdvancePayoutRunRequest.description: `completed`, `partially_failed` and `failed` are DERIVED from item outcomes and are deliberately not requestable: a run cannot be declared successful by assertion. Approval requires `payout_run:approve:organization`, which a migration assertion keeps disjoint from the preparer permission, AND a different membership from the one that prepared the run, AND recent step-up. An empty run cannot be approved, since that would create an authorisation with nothing under it for later items to fill.

SettlePayoutItemRequest.description: Debits the payable and credits cash for the net amount. The two accounts must differ.

PayoutItemSettled.description: The balanced entry and the paid status commit in ONE transaction, and the database refuses `paid` without a ledger entry, so the two cannot drift apart.

CreateSupportTicketRequest.description: The requester is the authenticated session and is never accepted from the body.

SupportTicketThread.description: Internal notes are excluded for a requester by the QUERY rather than filtered afterwards, so a serialization mistake cannot leak them. A caller who is neither the requester nor organization support staff receives 404, since confirming a ticket exists is itself a disclosure. Responses are no-store because a ticket body may contain anything a user typed.

internal_only.description: Support staff only. A requester marking their own message internal would hide it from the people meant to read it, so the flag is refused rather than silently ignored.

AssignSupportTicketRequest.description: A handover releases the current holder in the same transaction, so the one-active-assignment index expresses the change rather than refusing it.

AdvanceSupportTicketRequest.description: Closing requires a resolution first, so a ticket cannot be silently buried. A resolved ticket may be reopened to `in_progress`, because a requester saying it is not fixed is normal and forcing a new ticket would lose the history. Every transition appends an immutable status event.

RequestExportRequest.description: A bulk disclosure must say WHY. The purpose is retained with the job so an export can later be reviewed against the reason it was requested, and requesting one needs recent step-up.

downloadable.description: True only while the job is completed AND its file exists AND has not expired. Expiry is evaluated inside the query, so a caller cannot forget to compare it.

value.description: Any JSON value except null. jsonb `null` would defeat the NOT NULL column, so it is refused here and by a database CHECK.

PurchaseOrderStatus.description: `partially_received` and `received` are DERIVED from cumulative goods receipts against ordered quantity and are never requestable: a buyer must not be able to declare an order complete.

CreatePurchaseOrderRequest.description: The supplier must be active and belong to the acting organization, so an order cannot be raised against another tenant's supplier.

AddPurchaseOrderItemRequest.description: Lines are editable ONLY while the order is a draft, because approval must fix what was committed to. Cost is integer MYR sen.

AdvancePurchaseOrderRequest.description: An empty order cannot be submitted, since that would create an approvable commitment to buy nothing that later lines could quietly fill. Cancellation is refused once goods have physically arrived, because the stock is on the shelf and the ledger already records it.

ReceiveGoodsRequest.description: The lot and its expiry are required because FEFO picking depends on both; stock without an expiry cannot be ordered correctly. One batch per (site, variant, lot), so a second delivery of the same lot adds to the existing batch instead of creating a duplicate the picker would treat as separate stock.

GoodsReceiptCreated.description: The batch, the receipt and a POSITIVE ledger movement commit in one transaction. `inventory_batches` holds no quantity column — stock is a projection of posted movements minus active reservations — and `goods_receipts.movement_id` is NOT NULL, so a receipt cannot exist without the movement that made it real. Over-receipt is refused.

AddReturnItemRequest.description: The batch must belong to the same site as the return, otherwise a return could post stock into a branch that never held it.

AdvanceReturnRequest.description: Stock is posted back only on `completed`, which is reachable only once the goods are `received`. Each item posts at most once, guarded by its own `movement_id`, so a retried completion cannot double-credit stock.

ReconciliationCreated.description: Opening a reconciliation captures the EXPECTED quantity per batch as the ledger projects it at that instant. Comparing a physical count against a balance that moved afterwards would blame later dispatches on counting error.

RecordCountRequest.description: Zero is a legitimate count: an empty shelf is a finding, not a missing value. Counts are editable only while the reconciliation is a draft.

AdvanceReconciliationRequest.description: Approval requires a DIFFERENT person from the counter, enforced by a database CHECK as well as by the service: a stock count its own counter can approve is not a control, and an adjustment is exactly how shrinkage would be concealed. `posted` writes one signed adjustment movement per discrepant line.

ControlledRegister.description: One register per site and variant. Two registers for one controlled drug at one site would let the same stock be accounted twice, which is what a register exists to prevent. Requires pharmacy step-up per the policy matrix.

quantity_delta.description: Signed and non-zero: a controlled drug moves in or out, and zero is not a movement.

witness_profile_id.description: REQUIRED, and must be a different person from the actor. Migration 0024 documented the witness as mandatory while its CHECK permitted NULL, so dual control could be skipped by omitting the field; 0031 corrected the constraint and this mirrors it at the edge. Dual control one person can satisfy alone is not dual control.

ControlledMovementRecorded.description: The register entry and the stock ledger movement commit together and the entry names the movement, so the register and the ledger can never disagree about a controlled drug. The register events table is append-only by trigger. A movement that would leave the projection negative is refused, because that would mean the register accounts for stock that is not there — the exact condition it exists to surface.

WithdrawalStatus.description: The full catalogue vocabulary. Migration 0025 had created only five values; `under_review`, `processing` and `failed` were missing, and 0032 added them. Without `processing` there is no state for a transfer initiated but unconfirmed, so an in-flight payout would have to be recorded as not-started or already-paid — and recording an unconfirmed transfer as paid is how money goes missing unnoticed. `failed` is distinct from `rejected` because a bounced bank transfer is not an operator refusal.

RegisterBankAccountRequest.description: Requires driver step-up: redirecting a driver's earnings needs no other access, so this is the obvious account-takeover target. The number is accepted once, stored as a digest, and never returned; a new account supersedes the previous one, because two active accounts would make "where does this driver's money go" ambiguous at payout time.

BankAccountRegistered.description: Only the last four digits are ever echoed.

RequestWithdrawalRequest.description: Requires driver step-up. Evaluated in a SERIALIZABLE transaction because affordability is checked against a projection of the earnings ledger: two concurrent requests could each pass against the same balance and together exceed it — the same oversell shape as inventory, applied to money. A partial unique index independently permits one in-flight withdrawal per driver.

WithdrawalRequested.description: Available balance is earnings MINUS money already committed to an in-flight or completed withdrawal, so one balance cannot be withdrawn twice.

AdvanceWithdrawalRequest.description: A driver may only CANCEL their own request; every other transition needs `withdrawal:review:organization`, which a migration assertion keeps off the driver role, and the repository additionally refuses a reviewer whose PROFILE is the driver — one person holding both memberships would otherwise approve their own payout. Approval and settlement require step-up. Cancellation stops being available at `processing`, because the money may already have left. `rejected`, `cancelled` and `failed` require a reason code and nothing else may carry one. Settling posts a balanced ledger entry and binds it to the withdrawal in one transaction; the database refuses `paid` without a ledger entry.

InventoryBatch.description: Quantities are derived from the append-only stock ledger and active reservations.

StockMovement.description: Immutable stock ledger row; corrections are new movements, never edits.

DeliveryRating.description: Minimum-data rating; patient identity and free text are never exposed.

permission_id.description: The permission string following resource.subresource:action:scope grammar.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of what the permission grants, or null.

SupportTicketSummary.description: A queue row. Carries no message body: a ticket body is whatever a user typed, so including it in a list would widen exposure and make the response unbounded.

EmergencyEventSummary.description: A dispatch queue row. Carries the patient identifier and the location because a responder cannot be dispatched without them, and the route is gated on emergency.event:read:site. Carries NO vitals snapshot, triage notes or communications: those are per-event reads, and embedding them would widen exposure for every row an operator merely scrolls past. Coordinates are decimal strings, never floats, because re-serializing would change the stored value.

PayoutRunSummary.description: Totals are DERIVED from the run’s items in the same query, never stored on the run. A cached total that disagrees with its items is what makes a payout report untrustworthy, so this schema has nowhere to cache one.

LedgerEntrySummary.description: `amount_sen` is the sum of the POSITIVE postings, being the entry’s magnitude. This ledger stores signed amounts so a balanced entry sums to zero, and reporting that zero as the amount would make every transaction look like nothing happened. `balanced` is surfaced rather than assumed: an unbalanced entry cannot exist by constraint, so a false value would mean the invariant had been defeated and must be visible rather than hidden.

PurchaseOrderSummary.description: Quantities and totals are DERIVED from the lines and the receipts, never stored on the order: a stored total can disagree with the lines it claims to summarise. `outstanding_quantity` exists because a status of partially_received says nothing about how much is still missing.

StockReturnSummary.description: `posted_line_count` counts lines whose stock has already been put back. Without it a partially posted return looks complete from its status alone.

StockReconciliationSummary.description: `variance_quantity` is the SIGNED sum of counted minus expected and is the number a reconciliation exists to surface: direction matters, because missing stock and surplus stock are different problems. `absolute_variance_quantity` is carried alongside because a +50/-50 pair nets to zero while still being two counting errors, and a page showing only the net would call that clean. An approved or posted reconciliation always has an approver distinct from the counter, enforced by database constraint.

starting_within_24h.description: Appointments whose slot starts in the next 24 hours. A calendar day is deliberately not used: an organization has no stored timezone, so "today" could only be guessed.

active.description: Appointments still representing a live commitment: pending_payment, confirmed, checked_in or in_progress. Excludes rescheduled, whose replacement is counted instead.

organization_id.description: The organization the unit belongs to.

version.description: Semantic version of the firmware artifact.

current_version.description: The version the caller reported, or null when none was supplied.

latest_version.description: The newest published firmware for the profile, or null when none exists.

update_available.description: True when the latest version is newer than current_version (or current_version is unknown).

firmware_version.description: The latest firmware version when an update is available, otherwise null.

method.description: HTTP method the device must use to fetch the artifact.

url.description: Short-lived presigned URL for the firmware binary.

required_headers.description: Headers the device must send with the download request.
